practice_items.atom_title: Physical access controls (locks, badges, biometrics, mantraps)
practice_items.prompt: An administrator wants to prevent tailgating (where an unauthorized person follows an authorized person through a door). Which of the following physical access controls is the most effective solution for this specific threat?
options: A high-security biometric fingerprint scanner
A physical keyed deadbolt lock
A mantrap (access vestibule) with interlocked doors
An RFID badge reader with real-time audit logging
practice_items.explain: A mantrap features two interlocked doors where the second door cannot open until the first door closes, ensuring that only one person (or one authenticated party) can pass through per cycle, directly preventing tailgating. Badge readers and biometrics authenticate identity but do not physically block tailgating.

practice_items.atom_title: Physical access controls (locks, badges, biometrics, mantraps)
practice_items.prompt: Which of the following are distinct security advantages of an electronic RFID badge system over traditional mechanical keyed locks? (Select all that apply)
options: The ability to instantly revoke a user's access credentials in a central database without replacing physical hardware.
Complete immunity to credential cloning and signal sniffing attacks.
Automatic generation of an audit trail showing the timestamp and identity associated with each entry.
Independence from electrical power sources and network connectivity.
practice_items.explain: Electronic RFID badge systems allow administrators to revoke credentials instantly in a database, rendering the physical badge useless immediately. They also log each access event, creating a digital audit trail. However, they are vulnerable to signal cloning and generally rely on power and network connectivity.

practice_items.atom_title: Physical access controls (locks, badges, biometrics, mantraps)
practice_items.prompt: What is the common biometric performance metric that measures the probability that a system will incorrectly grant access to an unauthorized user?
practice_items.explain: The False Acceptance Rate (FAR) is the probability that a biometric security system will incorrectly authorize an unauthorized person.

practice_items.prompt: A facility relies entirely on CCTV cameras with no guards, alarms, or locks. Which statement BEST describes the limitation of this setup?
options: CCTV cannot record video at night under any circumstances
CCTV signals cannot be viewed remotely without a VCR
CCTV is a detective control; it can record an intrusion but cannot physically stop it
CCTV always requires a dedicated coaxial cable to function
practice_items.explain: Cameras document events (detective) but do not themselves prevent an intruder from breaching a fence or door; that requires preventive controls like locks and fencing plus a response process.

practice_items.prompt: An organization replaces its analog coaxial CCTV system with networked IP cameras. What is the PRIMARY new risk introduced by this upgrade?
options: IP cameras are now exposed to network-based attacks such as credential stuffing or firmware exploits
IP cameras cannot record footage for later review
IP cameras require more physical cabling than analog systems
IP cameras cannot support motion detection or analytics
practice_items.explain: Because IP cameras are addressable network devices, they inherit cyber risks (port scanning, default credentials, unencrypted RTSP sniffing, DoS) that an isolated analog coaxial loop is immune to.

practice_items.prompt: Which of the following are recommended mitigations for logical vulnerabilities in an IP camera network? Select ALL that apply.
options: Isolate cameras on a dedicated VLAN separate from general office traffic
Leave factory default admin credentials unchanged so support technicians can log in easily
Encrypt video streams in transit and at rest
Apply firmware updates to camera devices regularly
practice_items.explain: VLAN isolation, encryption, and firmware patching all reduce the attack surface. Leaving default credentials unchanged is the opposite of a mitigation, it is one of the most common ways attackers take over IP cameras.

practice_items.prompt: Give the term for an area within or around a facility that is not visible to any surveillance camera.
practice_items.explain: A blind spot is any unmonitored area; designers use overlapping fields of view between cameras to eliminate them.

practice_items.prompt: A security team watches live CCTV feeds on a monitor wall and dispatches a guard the moment they see a fence breach in progress. This is an example of:
options: Passive monitoring
Anti-passback
Thermal imaging
Active monitoring
practice_items.explain: Active monitoring means personnel watch live feeds in real time and can respond to an incident as it happens, unlike passive monitoring, which only reviews recorded footage after the fact.

practice_items.prompt: Why is passive-only monitoring (recording footage for later review, with no live viewing) considered insufficient on its own for stopping an attack in progress?
options: Passive monitoring uses more storage than active monitoring
Passive monitoring requires a live guard to be present at all times
Passive monitoring cannot be combined with thermal cameras
Passive monitoring only produces footage that is reviewed after an incident already occurred, so it cannot interrupt the attack itself
practice_items.explain: Passive/recorded monitoring is valuable for forensic investigation after the fact, but because no one is watching in real time, it does nothing to interrupt or prevent an attack while it is happening.

practice_items.prompt: Name the camera type that can be remotely swept across a wide area but temporarily creates a blind spot on the side it is not currently pointed toward.
practice_items.explain: A Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) camera offers wide coverage over time but, at any given instant, is only pointed at part of its range, the rest is a temporary blind spot.

practice_items.prompt: A guard at the reception desk denies entry to a visitor whose credentials look valid but whose story about their visit does not hold together under questioning. Which guard function does this best illustrate?
options: Patrol
Response
Reception and access verification
Visitor logging
practice_items.explain: Checking credentials and probing an inconsistent story at an entry point is the reception/access-verification role, something an automated badge reader cannot do.

practice_items.prompt: Which of the following are examples of a guard's response function? Select ALL that apply.
options: Physically investigating after a door sensor alarm fires
Walking a randomized route through the facility each shift
Responding in person when a camera detects motion in a restricted area after hours
Recording a visitor's name and sponsor in a log at the front desk
practice_items.explain: Response means physically investigating triggered alarms or detected motion. Randomized patrol routes are the patrol function, and recording visitor names is visitor-log administration, not response.

practice_items.prompt: A facility relies only on a badge reader at its single entrance. According to the defense-in-depth principle, what is the main weakness of this setup?
options: An attacker only needs to defeat one control (a cloned or stolen badge) to succeed
Badge readers are always unreliable hardware
Badge readers cannot log entry times
Badge readers require a network connection to function
practice_items.explain: With a single control layer, defeating that one layer is sufficient for an attacker. Defense-in-depth requires multiple independent categories so no single failure grants access.

practice_items.prompt: Why does adding a second security guard to the same reception desk NOT raise a facility's depth score?
options: Guards are never counted toward depth score
Two guards in the same personnel role duplicate an existing category rather than covering a new one
Depth score only counts electronic controls
A second guard actually lowers the depth score
practice_items.explain: Depth score counts distinct control categories, not total layers. A redundant personnel layer adds cost without closing a new gap that a different category (e.g., electronic or barrier) would close.

practice_items.prompt: Which of the following are true about mantraps? Select ALL that apply.
options: A mantrap uses two interlocking doors to prevent more than one person entering at a time
A mantrap by itself eliminates the need for any guard verification
A mantrap is most effective when paired with a guard who verifies identity on the far side
A mantrap is a barrier-category control
practice_items.explain: Mantraps are physical barrier controls that stop piggybacking, but they still benefit from a guard verifying identity in case of system error or ambiguous cases, they do not eliminate the value of human verification.

practice_items.prompt: Name the practice of following an authorized person through a controlled door without presenting your own credential.
practice_items.explain: Tailgating (also called piggybacking) is entering behind an authorized person without independently badging or verifying in.

practice_items.prompt: A visitor log records who entered a facility, their sponsor, and their arrival/departure times. Why is a visitor log alone NOT sufficient physical security?
options: Visitor logs are illegal to keep under most privacy laws
It is a deterrent and audit tool, not a barrier that stops unauthorized access in the moment
Visitor logs cannot record timestamps accurately
Visitor logs replace the need for an escort policy entirely
practice_items.explain: A visitor log creates accountability and an audit trail after the fact, but it does not physically prevent an unauthorized action from happening, it must be paired with escort policies and access controls.

practice_items.prompt: Why do data centers use clean-agent fire suppression (such as FM-200) instead of standard water sprinklers?
options: Clean-agent systems are cheaper to install than sprinklers
Water sprinklers are illegal in commercial buildings
Clean-agent systems require no maintenance
Water sprinklers destroy electronics on contact, even during a false activation
practice_items.explain: Water damages electronics immediately, and even a false sprinkler activation can write off an entire server room. Clean-agent systems extinguish fire without residue or equipment damage.

practice_items.prompt: A total utility power outage occurs. Which device responds first, within milliseconds, to keep servers running?
options: Backup generator
UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply)
Managed PDU
VESDA smoke detector
practice_items.explain: A UPS is a battery bank that responds in milliseconds, far faster than a generator can start, bridging the gap until the generator stabilizes or power is restored.

practice_items.prompt: Which of the following are functions of a backup generator in a data center power design? Select ALL that apply.
options: Provides extended runtime (hours to days) once started and stabilized
Responds within milliseconds of an outage, faster than a UPS
Typically starts and stabilizes within about 10 to 30 seconds
Is sometimes deployed in N+1 or 2N redundant configurations
practice_items.explain: Generators provide long runtime after a 10-30 second start delay, and critical facilities often run them in N+1 or 2N redundant configurations. A UPS, not a generator, is the millisecond-response layer.

practice_items.prompt: What is the purpose of hot aisle / cold aisle containment in a server room?
options: It reduces the noise level of HVAC equipment
It replaces the need for a fire suppression system
It prevents hot exhaust air from mixing with cool intake air, improving cooling efficiency and preventing hot spots
It increases humidity to prevent electrostatic discharge
practice_items.explain: Physical containment (curtains, doors, or roof panels) keeps cool intake air and hot exhaust air separated so cooling equipment can work efficiently and hot spots do not form.

practice_items.prompt: What does N+1 redundancy mean when applied to HVAC or power systems in a data center?
options: There is exactly enough capacity to meet current load with no margin
At least one extra unit of capacity exists beyond the minimum required, so a single unit failure does not cause an outage
Two completely separate, independently powered facilities are built
Redundant systems are tested once during initial installation only
practice_items.explain: N+1 redundancy means one extra unit of critical capacity (a spare generator, UPS, or HVAC unit) exists beyond the minimum needed, so a single failure does not cause a service outage.

practice_items.prompt: Name the early-warning smoke detection system that continuously samples air and can detect smoke particles well before a standard ionization detector would trigger.
practice_items.explain: VESDA (Very Early Smoke Detection Apparatus) samples air continuously, giving operators minutes of warning instead of seconds.

practice_items.prompt: A managed PDU (Power Distribution Unit) provides which capability that a basic power strip does not?
options: It generates its own backup power during an outage
It allows remote monitoring of per-outlet current and remote power cycling of individual devices
It cools the rack it is installed in
It suppresses fire at the rack level
practice_items.explain: A managed PDU supports remote monitoring and per-outlet control, allowing staff to remotely reboot a locked-up device without physically entering the restricted room.
